categories.title: Notice Writing

categories.title: Bio-Sketch (Biographical Sketch)
categories.description: A Bio-Sketch is a short, third-person analytical profile of a person built from factual cues, in a formal, informative tone.

formatTemplate.label: Name Heading
formatTemplate.guidance: Start with the full name of the person as a heading.

formatTemplate.label: Opening: Identity & Birth

formatTemplate.label: Body: Achievements
formatTemplate.guidance: Turn the given cues into smooth, connected sentences covering their career and major achievements.

formatTemplate.label: Tense & Perspective
formatTemplate.guidance: Use past tense for a deceased person, present/present-perfect for a living one — always third person ('He'/'She'), no personal opinions.

formatTemplate.label: Conclusion

categories.title: Letter to the Editor

categories.description: A formal letter to a newspaper editor raising civic, social, or environmental issues to build public awareness.

formatTemplate.label: Sender's Address & Date
formatTemplate.guidance: Write your address at the top left, followed by the date below it.

formatTemplate.label: Editor's Address & Subject
formatTemplate.guidance: Address it to 'The Editor', name of the newspaper, and city — then a one-line Subject stating the issue.

formatTemplate.label: Salutation
formatTemplate.guidance: Begin with 'Sir / Madam,'.

formatTemplate.label: Body Paragraph 1 — State the Problem
formatTemplate.guidance: Clearly describe the issue: what, where, and its nature.

formatTemplate.label: Body Paragraph 2 — Consequences
formatTemplate.guidance: Explain the effects or risks it causes to residents/students/the public.

formatTemplate.label: Body Paragraph 3 — Solution
formatTemplate.guidance: Suggest practical measures or request prompt action from the authorities.

formatTemplate.label: Closing
formatTemplate.guidance: End with a hopeful closing line, 'Yours sincerely,' and your full name.

categories.title: Story Writing (Given Cues / Outline / Title)
categories.description: Story Writing evaluates imagination, plot structuring, character development, and narrative flow, built from given cues, an outline, or a title.

formatTemplate.label: Catchy Title
formatTemplate.guidance: Give the story a short, engaging title.

formatTemplate.label: Introduction / Exposition
formatTemplate.guidance: Introduce the main character(s), setting, and initial scenario using engaging starter phrases or sensory details.

formatTemplate.label: Rising Action & Climax
formatTemplate.guidance: Introduce the central conflict, difficulty, or event; show action, presence of mind, or decision-making.

formatTemplate.label: Resolution & Conclusion
formatTemplate.guidance: Resolve the problem naturally and wrap up the narrative neatly.

formatTemplate.label: Moral
formatTemplate.guidance: End with a clear, one-line moral highlighting the core value, e.g. 'Honesty is the best policy.'

questions.title: The Lost Wallet
questions.description: Construct a story in 100–120 words using the outline provided below. Give your story a suitable title and a moral: A poor schoolboy finds a leather wallet on the playground... contains a large amount of cash and an ID card... tempted to buy shoes he always wanted... remembers his mother's advice on honesty... decides to hand it over to the Principal... owner turns out to be a chief guest... boy rewarded for integrity.

questions.title: The Test of Friendship
questions.description: Write an imaginative story in 100–120 words based on the given prompt. Assign an appropriate title and moral: Two close friends, Rohan and Soham, walking through a dark forest... hear a sudden roar... a bear approaches... Rohan quickly climbs a tall tree, leaving Soham behind... Soham remembers a lesson and lies still on the ground, holding his breath... bear sniffs him and walks away... Rohan comes down and asks what the bear whispered... Soham gives a fitting response.

questions.title: The Clever Thief and the Young Girl
questions.description: Develop a story in 100–120 words based on the given hints. Give a suitable title: Little Priya home alone on a rainy evening... hears suspicious noises near the back door... sees a stranger trying to pick the lock... panics at first but stays calm... slips into the kitchen... dials the police quietly... turns on loud music on the speaker to confuse the intruder... police arrive in time and apprehend the thief... Priya praised for bravery and presence of mind.

questions.title: The Stray Dog's Gratitude
questions.description: Write a short story in 100–120 words based on the following cues: A young boy named Aarav feeds an injured stray dog outside his house every day... names him 'Bruno'... months pass... one night, a small fire breaks out in the kitchen while the family is asleep... Bruno smells smoke and barks continuously outside the window... family wakes up just in time... fire put out safely... Bruno becomes a beloved hero.

questions.title: The Gift of a Pair of Shoes
questions.description: Create a narrative story in 100–120 words using the given outline: An energetic boy named Kabir loves playing football... notices an underprivileged barefoot boy watching him from outside the school field every afternoon... Kabir saves his pocket money for two months... buys a new pair of sports shoes... gifts them to the boy on his birthday... sees the priceless smile on his face... realizes true happiness lies in giving.

questions.title: The Strayed Bird
questions.description: Write a creative story in 100–120 words using the given hints: A young girl finds a small injured pigeon with a broken wing in her balcony... nurses it back to health with food, water, and bandages... builds a cozy box... bird recovers and learns to flutter again... girl feels attached and reluctant to let it go... realizes freedom is more precious... opens the cage and lets it fly into the sky.

questions.title: The Greedy Goose / Merchant
questions.description: Write a story in 100–120 words based on the classic outline below. Add a creative title and moral: A poor farmer owns a special goose... goose lays one golden egg every morning... farmer grows rich gradually... becomes impatient and greedy... wants all the golden eggs at once... kills the goose to search inside... finds nothing... loses both the goose and his source of wealth.

questions.title: The Woodcutter and the River Fairy
questions.description: Develop a story in 100–120 words using the provided cues: Honest woodcutter cutting wood near a river... axe slips and falls into deep water... woodcutter cries in distress... river goddess appears... offers an axe made of gold... woodcutter denies it is his... she offers a silver axe... he denies again... she finally brings his old iron axe... woodcutter happily accepts... goddess impressed by his truthfulness and rewards him with all three axes.

questions.title: An Unexpected Mystery
questions.description: Complete the story in 100–120 words starting with the given introductory sentence: "The old wooden door of the abandoned house slowly creaked open as the wind blew, revealing a glowing metallic box on the dusty floor..." Continue the story detailing what was inside the box, how the main character reacted, and how the adventure concluded. Give it a mysterious title.

questions.title: The Rainy Day Rescue
questions.description: Complete the story in 100–120 words beginning with the following line: "Heavy rain had flooded the street within an hour, and 12-year-old Dev was watching the rising water level from his porch when he noticed a tiny kitten stranded on a floating wooden plank..." Narrate how Dev managed to rescue the kitten safely, bring it home, and convince his parents to adopt it. Include a title and moral.

categories.title: Article Writing (School Magazine / Newspaper)
categories.description: An Article for a School Magazine or Student Newspaper expresses thoughts, opinions, and analysis on contemporary topics, school activities, or social issues.

formatTemplate.label: Catchy Title & Byline
formatTemplate.guidance: Give the article a catchy title, followed immediately by 'By: [Author's Name, Class & Section]'.

formatTemplate.label: Introduction
formatTemplate.guidance: Hook the reader with a general fact, rhetorical question, or strong opening statement, then introduce the core topic.

formatTemplate.label: Main Body
formatTemplate.guidance: Elaborate on the issue with specific facts, examples, or consequences, maintaining logical flow.

formatTemplate.label: Conclusion & Call to Action
formatTemplate.guidance: Offer practical solutions, positive recommendations, or a memorable concluding thought.

categories.title: Speech Writing
categories.description: A Speech is a formal address delivered verbally to an audience, such as during school morning assemblies, competitions, or special occasions.

formatTemplate.label: Suitable Title
formatTemplate.guidance: Give the speech a clear title matching its topic.

formatTemplate.label: Opening Address / Salutation
formatTemplate.guidance: Greet formally: 'Respected Principal, esteemed teachers, and my dear friends...', then introduce yourself and your topic.

formatTemplate.label: Introduction & Central Idea
formatTemplate.guidance: Hook the audience with a quote, question, or strong fact, then state the core thesis/topic clearly.

formatTemplate.label: Core Arguments & Examples
formatTemplate.guidance: Explain the significance, impact, or challenges connected to the topic using persuasive language ('We must remember...').

formatTemplate.label: Conclusion & Call to Action
formatTemplate.guidance: Summarize your main point in 1–2 inspiring sentences and end with a strong closing thought.

formatTemplate.label: Thank You
formatTemplate.guidance: Close with 'Thank you and have a wonderful day ahead!'

categories.title: Debate Writing (For / Against the Motion)
categories.description: A Debate presents a formal, logical argument for or against a stated motion, aimed at convincing an audience and judges of a specific viewpoint.

formatTemplate.label: Topic / Motion & Stance
formatTemplate.guidance: State the motion clearly, then declare whether you are speaking FOR or AGAINST it.

formatTemplate.label: Formal Salutation / Opening
formatTemplate.guidance: Greet formally: 'Respected Chairperson, honorable judges, worthy opponents, and dear audience...'.

formatTemplate.label: Stance Definition & Rhetorical Opening
formatTemplate.guidance: Define your stance clearly in sentence one, opening with a compelling fact, statistic, or rhetorical question.

formatTemplate.label: Core Arguments & Rebuttals
formatTemplate.guidance: Present 2–3 logical, well-structured arguments using persuasive signposts ('Furthermore...', 'My worthy opponents might argue that... however...').

formatTemplate.label: Strong Closing
formatTemplate.guidance: Summarize your core thesis forcefully and reiterate why your side holds the stronger ground.

formatTemplate.label: Thank You
formatTemplate.guidance: Close with 'Thank you!'

categories.title: Descriptive Paragraph (Person / Event / Place)
categories.subtitle: Set 2 — Detailed Cues
categories.description: A Descriptive Paragraph paints a vivid mental picture using sensory details (sight, sound, touch, smell, taste) and descriptive adjectives.

formatTemplate.label: Title
formatTemplate.guidance: Give the paragraph a short, fitting title.

formatTemplate.label: Opening/Topic Sentence
formatTemplate.guidance: Introduce the subject — person, event, or place — with an engaging overview.

formatTemplate.label: Supporting Details
formatTemplate.guidance: For a person: physical traits, mannerisms, clothing, key qualities, impact on others. For an event: chronological sequence, sights, sounds, emotional energy, climax. For a place: spatial layout, colors, atmosphere, sensory impressions.

formatTemplate.label: Vivid Language
formatTemplate.guidance: Use vivid adjectives (radiant, towering, bustling) and sensory imagery (petrichor, deafening cheer, gleaming marble) with smooth spatial/temporal transitions (adjacent to, gradually, as dusk fell).

formatTemplate.label: Concluding Sentence
formatTemplate.guidance: Summarize your overall feeling or lasting memory associated with the subject.

questions.title: My Favorite Teacher
questions.description: Write a descriptive paragraph in 100–120 words about your English teacher. Describe her physical appearance, tone of voice, teaching style, acts of kindness, and why she inspires you.

questions.title: A Grandparent / Wise Elder

questions.title: The Neighborhood Shopkeeper / Baker
questions.description: Write a descriptive paragraph in 100–120 words about a local baker or shopkeeper you visit regularly. Detail his appearance, friendly demeanor, the bustling atmosphere of his shop, and his interactions with customers.

questions.title: A Rainy Afternoon in My City

questions.title: A Local Cultural Festival / Fair

questions.title: A Fire Accident / Rescue Operation

questions.title: The School Library

questions.title: A Scenic Hill Station / Beach

questions.title: An Historical Monument
